- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward to reflect market resilience.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the next few days; apply a downward correction of 1–3% for the following 3–5 days.
- If model shows strong upward trend but sentiment is weak or neutral, expect mean reversion; reduce forecast slope or add downward bias.
- If model forecast is consistently higher than true outcome over 3–5 days, consider “lagged” bias — true price often lags model by 1–2 days; adjust forecast to align with 1–2 day lagged history.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive abruptly, model may misread momentum; delay upward adjustment by 1–2 days to avoid overreaction.
- For 30-day horizon, if model is consistently 2–3% above true outcome, reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 7–10 days unless sentiment confirms bullish momentum.
